question: According to management in Cloudflare's Q3 2024 earnings call, why did dollar-based net retention decline sequentially? Explain the cited drivers and distinguish them from a claim of increased churn.

answer.answer: On Cloudflare's Q3 2024 call (7 Nov 2024), CFO Thomas Seifert said dollar-based net retention was 110% in Q3 2024, down 2 percentage points sequentially. He attributed the decline to three things: (1) slower net expansion within the larger-customer cohort; (2) a greater mix of platform deals structured as 'pool of funds' contracts, which lower friction to adopting more products but change the shape/timing of revenue recognition (and affect deferred revenue and cash flow); and (3) lapping (anniversarying) the prior year's price increase on the PRO and Business PAYGO plans. In Q&A he added that pool-of-funds deals had risen to about 10% of new ACV booked in the quarter and would pressure DNR in the short term for roughly the next two to three quarters, while benefiting expansion over time. These are expansion-mix and revenue-recognition-timing drivers, not a claim of increased churn: the directly read passage attributes the decline to slower net expansion and deal structuring, and does not cite higher churn or higher attrition as a cause.
